inbox_items.title: Notification-router watchdog is dead and its marketing dead-flags are false positives
inbox_items.detail: notification-router/state.json was reachable this run. Its last_run is frozen at 2026-05-08T21:26Z (23 days stale) and the moteops_marketing.watchdog_dead flag (marketing-director, last_seen None, 19 consecutive sessions) was never resolved (resolved_at=None). Newest queue files date to 2026-05-17/18, so active dispatch stopped ~2 weeks ago. Meanwhile the VP agents ARE running — vp-tracking heartbeats exist for 05-28, 05-29, and 05-31. Conclusion: the watchdog that declared the marketing hierarchy 'dead' is itself stale/stopped; the dead-flag is a stale false positive, not evidence the VPs are down. Recommend: either restart the watchdog so it tracks the new scheduled-task heartbeats, or decommission it and clear the stale dead-flags so they stop polluting signal.

inbox_items.title: Router queue backlog persists uncleaned (~81k files)
inbox_items.detail: queue/expired holds 48,174 files and queue holds 33,045 files (~81,000 total). This matches the 05-28 count, confirming the backlog was never purged. Active flooding appears to have halted ~2026-05-17/18 (no newer files), so this is now a cleanup problem rather than an active runaway. Recommend purging both directories and confirming the cooldown/dedup fix landed before relying on router signal.

news.headline: Supabase made Data API auto-exposure opt-OUT the default for all NEW projects as of May 30 — public-schema tables now need explicit Postgres grants to be reachable via PostgREST/GraphQL. CoreVita Collective: any Supabase project you spin up after 5/30 returns empty from the Data API until you grant tables. Good for HIPAA posture, but bake the GRANTs into your migration template now so the next CoreVita env doesn't silently 404.
